reviewers.summary: The ANOVA analysis is methodologically sound in terms of basic execution, but critical reporting gaps and missing assumption checks undermine interpretability and reproducibility. Specifically, no effect size is reported despite available sums of squares, the homogeneity of variance assumption is unverified, the cohort is inadequately described, and there are contradictory statements about available estimates. These issues must be resolved before the manuscript can be promoted.

findings.title: No effect size reported despite available data
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: "No estimate-like records were available for p-value/effect-size checks."
stats-run.json: estimates include sum_sq (37.556 for group, 3093.747 residual)
findings.whyItMatters: The ASA statement discourages sole reliance on p-values. An effect size (e.g., eta-squared) is essential to interpret practical importance, especially with a non-significant p-value and a sample of 240.
findings.actionableFix: Compute and report eta-squared (or partial eta-squared) from the provided sums of squares: eta_sq = 37.556 / (37.556 + 3093.747). Also report a confidence interval if possible.

findings.title: Homogeneity of variance assumption not checked
evidenceRefs: diagnostics.json: only Shapiro-Wilk, VIF, leverage, Cook's D; no Levene's or Bartlett's test
manuscript.md: no mention of equal variance check
findings.whyItMatters: ANOVA assumes equal variances across groups. Without verification, the F-test may be invalid, especially if group sizes are unbalanced (unknown). A non-significant Shapiro-Wilk does not address this.
findings.actionableFix: Run Levene's test (or Bartlett's) on the residuals or original outcome by group, and report the result. If violated, consider Welch's ANOVA or transformation.

findings.title: Cohort definition insufficiently described
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: only states "240 complete-case records", no eligibility, group sizes, demographics, or source population
findings.whyItMatters: The lack of cohort detail makes it impossible to assess generalizability, potential confounding, or selection biases. It also hinders reproducibility and clinical interpretation.
findings.actionableFix: Add a clear cohort description: inclusion/exclusion criteria, how groups were defined, number per group, any relevant baseline characteristics (age, sex, etc.), and handling of missing data beyond complete-case exclusion.

findings.title: Inconsistent statement about estimate availability
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: "No estimate-like records were available for p-value/effect-size checks."
stats-run.json: contains F_statistic, p_value, and sum_sq
findings.whyItMatters: This contradictory statement misleads readers about the depth of available analysis and undermines trust in the quality control process.
findings.actionableFix: Update the limitations section to accurately reflect that effect size could have been computed but was not, or remove the incorrect sentence.

findings.title: Vague reference to unresolved advisory issues
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: "The methods review found advisory issues that need human review."
findings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot evaluate whether these issues affect the conclusion. Transparency requires specifying what advisory issues remain.
findings.actionableFix: Either list the specific advisory issues in the limitations or remove the statement if they have been resolved.

findings.title: Group variable categories not described
findings.whyItMatters: Without naming the groups, the clinical question "Does the continuous outcome differ across clinical groups?" is ambiguous.
findings.actionableFix: Define the group variable and its levels (e.g., control, enhanced treatment, standard treatment) in the manuscript.

findings.title: No exploration of missing data patterns
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: acknowledges complete-case exclusion may affect result, but no quantification
findings.whyItMatters: If missingness is non-trivial and related to outcome or group, bias may be introduced. The absence of any missingness analysis weakens the robustness of findings.
findings.actionableFix: Report the number of excluded records, compare demographics between included and excluded if data allow, or state that missingness was minimal (<5%) and presumed random.

missingEvidence: manuscript-qa.json content not provided in artifact packet
Raw data not available to verify group sizes, actual variable coding, or missingness patterns
No post-hoc power analysis or justification for sample size

reviewers.summary: The ANOVA analysis is incomplete: missing crucial assumption check (homogeneity of variances), no effect size, no descriptive statistics, unclear missingness handling, and other minor reporting gaps. Revision required.

findings.title: No test for homogeneity of variances is reported
findings.whyItMatters: ANOVA assumes equal variances across groups; violation can inflate Type I error rates.
findings.actionableFix: Report Levene's test or Bartlett's test; if violated, consider Welch's ANOVA or robust methods.

findings.title: No effect size (e.g., eta-squared) reported
findings.whyItMatters: A p-value alone does not convey the magnitude of group differences; effect size is essential for interpretation.
findings.actionableFix: Compute and report eta-squared or omega-squared from the ANOVA output.

findings.title: Group-level descriptive statistics not provided
findings.whyItMatters: Without means and standard deviations, readers cannot assess direction, magnitude, or data plausibility.
findings.actionableFix: Add a table of N, mean, SD, and optionally 95% CI for each group.
findings.deterministicVerification: Could be verified from raw data if available.

findings.title: No description of missing data or exclusion criteria
findings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis can bias results if missingness is not random; the extent and reasons for exclusion need documentation.
findings.actionableFix: Report the number of records excluded, reasons for missingness, and consider sensitivity analysis (e.g., pattern-mixture) or explicitly acknowledge limitation.

findings.title: Figure not referenced or described in manuscript
findings.whyItMatters: Included figures enhance understanding, but if unmentioned, they do not contribute to the narrative.
findings.actionableFix: Include the figure in the manuscript with a descriptive caption and in-text reference.

findings.title: No prior literature or clinical context discussed
findings.whyItMatters: Lack of contextualization makes the novelty and relevance of the findings unclear.
findings.actionableFix: Briefly mention related studies or the clinical rationale for examining the outcome across these groups.

findings.title: No analysis script or raw data provided for independent reproduction
findings.whyItMatters: Reproducibility is a core principle; without code and data, results cannot be independently verified.
findings.actionableFix: Include a script (e.g., R/Python) that reproduces the analysis from the raw data, or provide a reproducibility package.

findings.title: Group sample sizes not reported; possible imbalance unknown
findings.whyItMatters: Unbalanced designs can affect ANOVA’s robustness to assumption violations and power; readers need to know group sizes.
findings.actionableFix: Report the number of observations per group.

missingEvidence: Levene's test or Bartlett's test result for homogeneity of variances
Descriptive statistics (mean, SD) for each group
Missing data details (number of exclusions, reasons)
Analysis script and raw data for reproducibility assessment

reviewPanel.nextAction: Adjudicate findings and route accepted repairs back into the pipeline.
